source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative found in Sun Pharma's FY25 disclosures/press releases; growth commentary centers on US specialty portfolio (Global Specialty ~20% of revenue), India branded generics (+13.7%), and Emerging Markets/RoW formulations rather than China-sourcing diversification.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment mix (US Formulations 31%, Emerging Markets 18%, RoW 14%, API & Others 4%) implies ~67% of consolidated revenue (Rs 54,543 cr total) is foreign-currency linked, predominantly USD. Specific hedging/forward-contract policy language could not be located; company AR PDF returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries was named among the Group A approved applicants (high-value complex/patented products category) under the Government of India's Rs 15,000 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals.

china_plus_one.evidence: Alkem is a predominantly domestic-focused branded generics company (~70% of FY25 revenue from India); no China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found in earnings commentary. Management noted international business 'excluding the Americas' is seeing good traction but framed this as market expansion, not China-related de-risking.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~30% of FY25 revenue (Rs 1,34,583 mn total) is international/export business, partly USD-linked (includes US generics business, which management flagged as facing price erosion). No specific hedging/forward-contract policy quote located; AR PDFs returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alkem was not identified by name in the Group A list of the Rs 15,000 crore PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (named beneficiaries: Sun Pharma, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Lupin, Cadila, Cipla, Glenmark, Torrent) nor among the 19 approved beneficiaries of the API/bulk-drug KSM/DI PLI scheme found via search; participation status could not be confirmed from available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: "China+1 strategy and the US Biosecure Act to reduce dependency and diversify supply chain with dual sourcing place India as a reliable partner" - the Custom Synthesis segment's 'strong resurgence,' with 'several Big Pharma projects transitioning into full-scale production,' is directly attributed to global pharma's China+1/de-risking sourcing shift and Biosecure Act tailwinds, coinciding with FY25 consolidated revenue growth of 19% to Rs 9,712 cr.

inr_exposure.evidence: 88% of FY25 sales revenue derived from exports (Europe ~56%, North America ~16%, other geographies ~16%), implying high foreign-currency (USD/EUR) revenue exposure. Specific hedging/forward-contract policy text not located; AR PDF returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories does not appear among the 19 approved beneficiaries of the Rs 6,940 crore PLI scheme for API/KSM/Drug-Intermediate bulk drugs, nor in the named Group A/B beneficiary lists of the Rs 15,000 crore PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals. The company is instead expanding CDMO/API capacity organically (e.g., Kakinada complex) via long-term supply agreements with Big Pharma rather than disclosed PLI incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative located in accessible FY25 disclosures. Lupin's growth commentary centers on complex generics (55% of EMEA regional revenue), specialty/biosimilars pipeline, and steady US (+13.5% to USD 925 mn) and India (34% of sales) growth rather than a China-sourcing diversification framing.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 geographic mix: US 36%, India 34%, Other Developed Markets (Canada/Australia/Europe) ~13%, Emerging Markets (LATAM/South Africa/Philippines/RoW) ~11%, implying ~66% of revenue is foreign-currency denominated (predominantly USD, also EUR/GBP/CAD/AUD). Specific hedging/forward-contract policy quote not located; Integrated Report PDF returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin Limited was named among the Group A approved applicants under the Government of India's Rs 15,000 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (high-value complex/patented products category).

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 / supply-chain diversification framing found in available sources. FY25 segmental revenue: Domestic Rs 2,269 Cr, International Rs 1,128 Cr, CDMO Rs 446 Cr, API Rs 76 Cr; international formulations growth (~6%) attributed to Russia and branded generics exports, not to diversification-from-China narrative.

inr_exposure.evidence: International business (~42% of FY25 revenue, spanning Russia/CIS, South Africa, branded generics exports and CDMO) implies material foreign-currency exposure, but no explicit USD-specific quantification or hedging/forward-contract policy quote was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: JB Chemicals operates a small API segment (~Rs 76 Cr, ~2% of FY25 revenue) but no source found confirming it is a named beneficiary under the Government's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs.

china_plus_one.evidence: Zydus MD Sharvir Patel publicly stated that '60% of medicines consumed in the US are made in India,' underscoring India's role in US generics supply, but this was not framed in available sources as an explicit China+1 diversification narrative tied to Zydus's own revenue/order growth.

inr_exposure.evidence: US formulations business is described as contributing roughly 47% of consolidated revenues (a key revenue driver, ~12% YoY segment growth cited for FY24); no specific forward-contract/hedging policy quote was located. Consumer Wellness (largely India-domestic) was ~14% of revenue in FY25 per available snippets, though this figure could not be fully reconciled to full-year totals.

pli_scheme.evidence: Zydus has API/bulk-drug operations (including an SBL API business acquisition) but no source found explicitly confirming PLI scheme beneficiary status or associated revenue percentage.

china_plus_one.evidence: Torrent has pursued API backward integration (Glochem Industries API unit acquisition, Dahej and Indrad capacity) described as reducing 'input cost vulnerability' and securing supply chains; this reflects the broader industry China+1/API self-reliance trend but was not found explicitly framed by Torrent itself as a China+1 narrative driving revenue growth.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix: India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, Other markets 15% -- implying ~45% multi-currency (USD/BRL/EUR and others) exposure via international operations. No specific hedging/forward-contract policy quote was located in available sources; India is also ranked No.1 among Indian pharma companies in Brazil and Germany.

pli_scheme.evidence: No source found explicitly confirming Torrent Pharmaceuticals as a named PLI scheme beneficiary; its API self-sufficiency efforts (Glochem, Dahej) appear to be internally funded backward integration rather than PLI-linked.

china_plus_one.evidence: Gland Pharma (majority owned by China's Fosun Pharma) is itself an India-based injectables/API exporter to the US, Europe, and Australia, and is frequently cited in industry commentary as a beneficiary of the broader China+1 sourcing shift; however, no explicit quote from Gland's own annual report or management framing this as a China+1-driven growth narrative was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: US market share of revenue cited at 54% (with 27% YoY US sales growth) and Europe (via Cenexi) revenue smaller in the figures found (~5% in the period reported); India domestic revenue reported as roughly flat and very small (~1% of revenue). Figures appear to derive from a quarterly (Q4FY25) press release rather than confirmed full-year totals. No specific hedging/forward-contract policy quote was located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Gland Pharma manufactures in Andhra Pradesh, one of the states with an approved PLI Bulk Drug Park, but no source found explicitly confirms Gland Pharma itself as a named PLI scheme beneficiary or discloses an associated revenue percentage.

china_plus_one.evidence: Mankind Pharma is an almost entirely India-domestic branded generics/formulations company; no export-diversification or China+1 narrative found. Exports are a small but fast-growing part of the business (H1 FY25 exports Rs 540 Cr vs domestic Rs 5,430 Cr of Rs 5,970 Cr total revenue from operations), but this growth is attributed to international formulations/API expansion, not China+1 supply-chain shifts.

rural.evidence: FY25 city-class sales mix: Metro 34%, Town Class 1 23%, Town Class 2-6 23%, Rural 19% (Metro & Tier-1 combined ~55-57%). Mankind has one of the deepest rural/Tier 2-3-4 distribution networks among Indian pharma companies.

inr_exposure.evidence: Predominantly domestic (~90%) revenue base implies limited FX/USD exposure; no explicit hedging policy quote found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that Mankind Pharma is a listed beneficiary under the PLI Bulk Drugs (KSM/API) scheme or PLI Pharmaceuticals scheme; company is primarily a formulations/branded generics player rather than a large-scale API/bulk-drug manufacturer targeted by these schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: Natco is a globally export-oriented generics/API company (finished dosage formulations marketed in 50+ countries incl. US, Canada, Brazil, Europe; major US partners include Sun Pharma, Teva, Mylan/Viatris, Lupin, Dr. Reddy's) but no explicit China+1 or supply-chain-diversification-from-China narrative was found tied to revenue/order growth.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export formulation business (predominantly US, Canada, Brazil, Europe) accounted for ~85% of FY25 revenue (revenue from operations Rs 4,784 Cr in FY25 vs Rs 4,127 Cr FY24), implying substantial USD/foreign-currency revenue exposure. No explicit hedging/forward-contract policy quote located in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Natco Pharma is one of 9 domestic companies approved under Group B of the PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (incentive ceiling of Rs 2,250 Cr for Group B); specific incentive amount received or revenue contribution not disclosed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar operates manufacturing/assembly plants across India, US, Mexico and China, and its AR/MD&A frames continuous product-platform-geography diversification as a deliberate resilience strategy: "Diversification has been their way of building resilience... reducing concentration risks while creating new opportunities in emerging mobility ecosystems." No explicit 'China+1' phrase found, and the company is also separately expanding INTO the China EV market, so this is export/geography diversification framing rather than an explicit China+1 customer-relocation narrative.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue split ~29% India / ~71% exports, with North America alone at 41%; remainder from Europe (~24%, derived residual) and rest-of-Asia (6%). Majority of export revenue is USD/foreign-currency denominated, indicating meaningful FX exposure. No explicit forward-contract/hedging policy quote located in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto-component maker certified under the Auto PLI scheme, initially for a hub-wheel-drive motor for electric two-wheelers, and subsequently received certification for three EV traction motors (August 2025); specific revenue contribution/incentive amount not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch Limited India's FY25 commentary notes export sales growth within the Powertrain Solutions division (5.8% segment sales increase driven by tractor segment and exports), but no specific export percentage or China+1/supply-chain diversification narrative was found in available (non-AR-PDF) sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Bosch Limited (subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH) has a growing export component within its Mobility Solutions business (notably Powertrain Solutions), implying some foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no percentage figure or hedging policy quote was found in available sources (full AR PDF and bosch.in were inaccessible - HTTP 403).

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch was approved under the Component Champion category of the Auto PLI scheme in March 2022 (one of ~74-82 approved companies). Actual incentive receipt/revenue contribution specifically for listed Bosch Limited (BSE 500530) vs. group entities is unconfirmed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China-linked manufacturing/export narrative found. IHCL is a domestic-led hospitality company; management commentary (FY25 results, press releases) frames growth around Indian tourism demand, not China-plus-one supply-chain dynamics.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Secondary sources (ICICI Direct note, Sep 2024) indicate IHCL has 'minimal significant debt except lease liabilities' and has remained conservative on borrowings since its equity infusion in FY2022, implying low overall leverage. Exact floating-vs-fixed rate debt split was not found; the underlying Annual Report PDF could not be fetched (403 errors).

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL earns management/license fee income and revenue from international hotels and JVs (e.g., The Pierre New York, Taj Boston, Taj Cape Town, and properties in the UK, Maldives, Sri Lanka), implying some USD/foreign-currency revenue. FY25 total management fees were reported at ~Rs 562 crore (up 18.7% YoY), but this combines domestic and international contracts and is not broken out by currency. Management stated 80-90% of future growth will still come from within India. No explicit USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Hospitality sector; not a PLI scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China-linked manufacturing/export narrative found; NAM-India is a domestic asset management company with a small offshore fund business, unrelated to China-plus-one supply chain themes.

rural.evidence: Not directly disclosed as 'rural revenue,' but Nippon India Mutual Fund discloses a B30 (beyond-top-30-cities) AUM split as a semi-urban/rural-reach proxy: as of FY25, T30 city AUM was ~Rs 4.45 lakh crore and B30 city AUM ~Rs 1.41 lakh crore, with the company cited among the top 5 fund houses by B30 AUM. This is an AUM proxy, not a revenue percentage, so revenue_pct is left null.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Asset management companies typically carry minimal borrowings; no floating/fixed debt disclosure found or expected to be material.

inr_exposure.evidence: NAM India runs an offshore/international business via NAM Singapore and GIFT City. As of March 31, 2025, NAM Singapore managed ~USD 1.78bn in offshore managed AUM plus ~USD 233mn in international advisory mandates, versus total company AUM of ~Rs 6,54,112 crore (~USD 78bn) - offshore AUM is roughly low-single-digit percent of total AUM. This generates some USD-denominated fee revenue, but an explicit USD revenue % or hedging policy was not disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Financial services/AMC; not a PLI scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China-linked manufacturing/export narrative found; Radico's export markets cited are UK, US, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and Hong Kong, unrelated to China-plus-one supply-chain themes.

rural.evidence: Multiple broker/industry notes cite rising rural income and consumption, and conversion from illicit/toddy liquor to IMFL, as structural demand drivers for the Indian IMFL industry (and by extension Radico), but no explicit rural revenue percentage was found disclosed by Radico specifically in accessible secondary sources.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No specific floating-vs-fixed debt disclosure found in accessible secondary sources; the Annual Report PDF could not be fetched directly (403 error).

crude_exposure.evidence: Key inputs are grain/ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass bottles. Industry commentary (e.g., Sharekhan note) flags volatility in grain, ENA and glass bottle costs, with glass bottle prices up 12-20% and overall packaging costs up 30-40% in recent periods amid input cost inflation. No explicit raw-material-as-%-of-revenue figure or direct crude-oil linkage was disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico derives ~8-9% of revenue (and ~4-5% of volume) from exports to ~100 countries (UK, US, Europe, Middle East, Africa, SE Asia, Australia/NZ, Singapore, Hong Kong), implying modest USD/GBP/EUR-denominated revenue, but exact USD revenue % and any hedging policy were not disclosed in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcoholic beverages sector is not a PLI scheme category; no evidence of PLI participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China-linked manufacturing/export narrative found; Phoenix Mills is a purely domestic mall/retail/office/residential real estate developer and operator.

rural.evidence: Not applicable - Phoenix Mills operates malls, offices and residential projects in major Indian metros/tier-1 cities; no rural revenue disclosure.

govt_capex.evidence: No explicit government infrastructure revenue linkage found; Phoenix Mills is a private mall/retail real estate developer and operator with no disclosed government-capex-linked revenue stream.

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 saw significant deleveraging: consolidated long-term debt fell from ~Rs 38bn (FY24) to ~Rs 7bn (FY25), with debt-to-equity down to ~0.1x from ~0.4x. Q2FY25 disclosures cited an average cost of debt of 8.67%, group gross debt of Rs 4,379 crore, net debt of Rs 2,405 crore, and net debt/EBITDA of 1.1x. Borrowings are typically a mix of floating (repo/MCLR-linked) and fixed-rate instruments, but no explicit floating-vs-fixed percentage split was found - AR and investor presentation PDFs could not be fetched directly (403 errors).

inr_exposure.evidence: No foreign-currency/USD revenue exposure found; business is entirely INR-denominated domestic real estate leasing and retail operations.

pli_scheme.evidence: Real estate/retail sector is not a PLI scheme category; no evidence of PLI participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: IKS Health is a healthcare BPO/KPO serving US healthcare providers with delivery centers based in India (Navi Mumbai HQ); no China exposure or China+1 manufacturing-diversification narrative found. No disclosed narrative about diversifying delivery centers away from a single non-India geography either.

rural.evidence: Not applicable - IKS Health's revenue is derived entirely from US-based healthcare provider clients (B2B services export from India), with no rural India revenue stream.

govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable - company has no exposure to Indian government capex programs; it is a healthcare services exporter to US clients.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No specific disclosure on floating-rate debt found in available sources. As an asset-light services/BPO company that recently listed (IPO Dec 2024) with reportedly strong cash generation, debt levels are likely low, but this could not be confirmed from primary sources within the fetch budget.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable - IKS Health is a services company (healthcare BPO/KPO) with no raw material or crude-linked input costs.

inr_exposure.evidence: Multiple secondary sources indicate IKS Health derives revenue entirely from international markets, specifically US healthcare provider clients, i.e., ~100% USD-denominated revenue with 0% domestic India revenue. FY25 revenue was reported at approximately Rs 2,664 crore (up 47% YoY), all sourced from US clients. Could not access primary annual report/IR PDF to confirm exact disclosed hedging/forward-contract policy - this remains unconfirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable - PLI (Production Linked Incentive) schemes target manufacturing sectors; IKS Health is a healthcare services/BPO exporter with no manufacturing operations, so it is not a PLI beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 supply-chain diversification narrative found. Titan is a domestic B2C jewellery/watch/eyewear retailer (Tanishq, Titan watches, CaratLane, Eyewear); it is not positioned as a manufacturing exporter benefiting from China+1 sourcing shifts.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural/Tier-2/Tier-3 revenue percentage was found. Qualitative evidence is strong: Tanishq has been explicitly expanding into Tier-2/Tier-3 towns via franchisee model, with reporting that Tanishq had 350+ stores across 200+ Indian cities and plans to add 200+ outlets in ~130 new small towns over 5 years, citing that small-town/rural consumers buy more jewellery per capita than metro consumers. No hard % figure disclosed in the sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable - Titan is a B2C consumer retailer (jewellery, watches, eyewear) with no meaningful government/infrastructure capex-linked revenue stream identified.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Could not access Titan's annual report notes-to-accounts to confirm floating vs. fixed rate borrowing mix. No figure found via search.

crude_exposure.evidence: Titan's core raw materials are gold, diamonds, and silver (jewellery division, ~91%+ of revenue), which are not crude-oil-linked. No disclosure found tying eyewear plastics/packaging costs to crude/petrochemical prices as a %.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue is predominantly India-domestic/INR. Titan does have a small and growing international jewellery footprint (Tanishq/Mia international stores - ~23 stores including Singapore, GCC, and North America as of FY25), but no % of total revenue was disclosed for this international segment. Note: Titan imports gold as a raw material, creating USD-linked COST exposure (not revenue exposure), but no explicit hedging policy percentage was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that Titan participates in any India PLI scheme. Jewellery, watches, and eyewear retail/manufacturing are not among the sectors covered by India's PLI schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: No news, investor presentation, or annual-report coverage found mentioning supply-chain/sourcing diversification away from China for Nykaa's private-label products. Nykaa is a domestic consumer e-commerce/retail company, not a manufacturer or exporter, so a China+1 narrative is not applicable to its business model.

rural.evidence: No consolidated FY2024-25 revenue_pct for Tier 2/3/smaller-town contribution was found in an official filing. However, multiple secondary sources report that Nykaa Fashion now derives roughly 60% of its sales from Tier 2 and smaller cities, and that Nykaa has expanded its offline footprint to ~200-250 stores across ~72+ Indian cities by FY25. This figure pertains to the Fashion vertical/offline stores specifically, not disclosed as a total-company revenue percentage, hence left null.

govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable / not disclosed. Nykaa is a B2C beauty/fashion e-commerce and retail company with no exposure to government capex or infrastructure spending programs.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No explicit floating-rate-liability percentage was found. Secondary sources note finance costs rose ~29.5% YoY in FY25 and that subsidiary Nykaa Fashion Limited has term loans from ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank totaling over Rs 70 crore, but the interest-rate structure (floating vs fixed) was not disclosed in accessible sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: No explicit raw-material-to-crude-oil linkage percentage disclosed. Nykaa's private-label beauty products likely use plastic/petrochemical-derived packaging, but this exposure is not quantified in any available disclosure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue is predominantly INR-denominated from Indian domestic operations. One notable minor international development: Nykaa's owned brand Kay Beauty made its international retail debut at Space NK in the UK during FY25, but this is not disclosed as a quantified USD/GBP revenue percentage, and no hedging policy was found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nykaa operates as an e-commerce marketplace and retailer of beauty/fashion/wellness products; India's PLI schemes target manufacturing sectors, not e-commerce/retail services, so Nykaa is not expected to be a PLI beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit 'China+1' or de-risking language found in company sources (Usha Martin's own AR/IR PDFs were unreachable, all returning 403). However, third-party analyst commentary links the government's PLI scheme for specialty steel/wire products to a 'favourable backdrop' for Usha Martin's Steel Wire Ropes and Wire Products segment, an initiative aimed at import substitution and reducing reliance on Chinese/imported specialty steel. This is adjacent to a China+1 narrative but not a direct company statement about customers diversifying away from Chinese wire-rope suppliers toward Usha Martin.

rural.evidence: Usha Martin is a B2B industrial wire rope / specialty steel manufacturer serving mining, oil & gas, infrastructure, elevators and cranes; no rural/consumer revenue exposure is applicable or disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Company materials and press describe key end markets as mining, oil & gas, infrastructure/construction (bridges, flyovers, metro rail), elevators and cranes, with Coal India Limited cited as a marquee customer. International revenue (57% of FY25 sales) is also described as driven by 'oil and gas, mining, and infrastructure' demand. However, no explicit revenue percentage tied to government/PSU/infrastructure end-markets was found - the actual Annual Report PDFs returned HTTP 403 and could not be read directly, so this is qualitative only.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Usha Martin is a capital-intensive integrated steel/wire-rope manufacturer and plausibly carries term loans and working-capital debt, but the notes-to-accounts disclosure on floating vs. fixed-rate borrowings could not be retrieved - all annual report PDF links returned HTTP 403 in this environment, and Screener.in was also blocked (403).

crude_exposure.evidence: Usha Martin's primary raw materials are steel wire rod, billets, iron ore and coking coal (captive mines in Jharkhand), not crude oil or petrochemicals. No disclosure was found tying any raw material cost to crude oil pricing; marking not applicable.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export markets contributed 57% of FY25 consolidated revenue (Rs 3,474 crore total), spanning Europe (25%), Asia Pacific (14%), Middle East & Africa (10%) and Americas (8%) - much of this is plausibly USD- or EUR-denominated, but an explicit 'USD revenue %' and the current forex hedging/forward-contract policy from notes to accounts could not be confirmed since the Annual Report PDFs were unreachable (403 errors).

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (Rs 6,322 crore outlay, approved 2021, with subsequent rounds PLI 1.1 in Jan 2025 and PLI 1.2 in Feb 2026) targets categories including alloy steel wires, directly relevant to Usha Martin's product range. Analyst commentary on Usha Martin's FY25 results states the 'PLI scheme continuity...creates a favourable backdrop' for its Steel Wire Ropes and Wire Products operations, implying sector-level benefit, but no source found explicitly confirms Usha Martin as a signed/registered PLI beneficiary company or quantifies any PLI-linked revenue, so is_beneficiary is left conservatively false.
